transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is… I just can’t keep my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore, even when it really matters. Like at work, I’ll be tracing a client’s network problem, looking through logs, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve read the same few entries three times and I still couldn’t tell you what they said.

And then I start thinking maybe it’s the firewall, or maybe it’s something I saw on a different ticket last month—actually there was this one router issue that took forever—but, sorry, the point is I’m not staying with what’s in front of me. It’s getting bad enough that I’m worried about messing things up.
Do you ever feel restless or find yourself needing to move around when you’re trying to focus on something?

Yeah, definitely. Even when I’m supposed to just sit still and listen, it feels like there’s this… motor humming under my skin or something. Like I need to stand up, check something, move to the next problem right that second.

It’s not always that I actually get up—though sometimes I do—but it’s like my body is already trying to leave before my brain has finished with the thing in front of me.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus on something important?

Yes. Very much. Especially at home, because everything is right there, you know? I’ll be trying to work on one machine or one ticket, and then the dishwasher clicks or beeps, or a neighbor walks past the window, and that’s it — I’m gone.

Or sometimes it’s not even something outside. I’ll suddenly think, wait, there’s that other computer I meant to fix, or that update I should check, and before I realize it I’ve completely left the job I was supposed to be doing. Then I come back and I’m like… what was I even looking at?
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse without thinking things through, like making sudden decisions or interrupting others before they finish speaking?

Yeah… I do. More than I’d like to admit. Especially when it’s something technical, because the answer sort of pops into my head before the other person is done explaining.

Like someone will be describing a computer issue, and I already think I know what it is, so I’ll cut in and start talking over them. Or worse, if I’m next to them, I’ll just reach for the keyboard and start doing the thing before they’ve finished telling me what happened. And sometimes I’m right, but that doesn’t really matter because it’s rude, and I know that while I’m doing it.

It’s like my mouth or my hands get ahead of the part of me that’s supposed to wait.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m not exactly cheerful, but “down” or “depressed” feels like a strong word.

And the “lost interest” part… I don’t know. I still do the things I normally do, at least I think I do. Two weeks is hard for me to judge because days kind of blur together. I haven’t specifically noticed, like, suddenly not caring about things I usually enjoy. But I also haven’t been tracking it, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when you know they might not be that big of a deal, and does it feel hard to control those worries once they start?

I don’t know if I’d call it worrying a lot. I mean, I think about things, sure — like if something at work is going to turn into a bigger mess than it looks like, or if I forgot to follow up with someone. But then again, that’s kind of the job, right? Computers always have some hidden problem underneath the obvious one.

The “hard to control” part… I’m not sure. Sometimes a thought keeps looping, but I don’t know if that’s worry exactly or just me trying to solve something in my head. Like I’ll be making coffee and suddenly I’m thinking about a printer issue from three days ago, and then I remember I need filters, and then somehow I’m checking whether the router firmware got updated. So… I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as worry versus just my brain running off with a thread.
Over the past two weeks, have you noticed feeling tired or having little energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s “most days” or just normal tired, you know?

Like, if I’m sitting at a computer too long, I’ll feel kind of drained, but then that happens to everyone staring at screens. And sometimes I’ll think I’m tired, but then I get up to do something else and I’m fine. Or I start messing with one little thing on the computer and suddenly an hour’s gone by, so I guess I had energy for that.

So… I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern of having little energy for no reason. I’d have to pay closer attention to answer that better.
Looking back, would you say you've had trouble staying focused and felt restless or overly active for most of your life, even going back to when you were a child or teenager?

Yeah, I mean… going back, my mother would probably answer that faster than I can. She still jokes about my grade school report cards saying I was “bright,” but then there’d be all this other stuff about how I wouldn’t stay in my seat, or I’d call out answers before I was supposed to.

And the homework thing too — apparently I’d lose it even when I’d actually done it, which is still kind of funny, or not funny, depending on who you ask. I remember school folders being this whole disaster area. But yeah, that goes way back.
